Derivative-Free Optimization 7: The Pattern Search Minimiser¶

Pattern search is the method behind constrained derivative-free problems in the facade. Called directly with pattern_search_minimizer, it exposes the poll, the search step, the mesh, linear constraints written as matrices, and three policies for nonlinear constraints. After this chapter you can choose each of these deliberately and read the diagnostics that tell you what the run did.

Every program is complete and its output is the output of that program. Counts are evaluations of the objective.

The method¶

Pattern search keeps a mesh size and a best point. Each iteration:

  1. Search (optional). Try a few extra points chosen to jump ahead. If one improves, accept it and skip the poll.

  2. Poll. Evaluate points at distance mesh along a set of directions around the best point. If one improves, move there and grow the mesh by mesh_expansion.

  3. If nothing improves, shrink the mesh by mesh_contraction.

The run ends with Converged when the mesh is below mesh_tolerance and the last step or value change was small. Because the poll directions positively span the space, a failed poll at a small mesh says no direction improves the point at that scale, which is the derivative-free analogue of a zero gradient.

With constraints, the directions are adapted to the constraints active at the current point, and the feasible cone’s edges are added to the poll, so the method can slide along a face and leave a vertex.

The call¶

PSOutcome pattern_search_minimizer(objective, initial, PSConfig config = {});

PSConfig group

Fields

Defaults

tolerances

mesh_tolerance, step_tolerance, value_tolerance, constraint_tolerance

1e-6 each

budgets

max_iterations (0 = 100 × variables), max_evaluations (0 = 2000 × variables), time_limit_seconds

0, 0, none

mesh

initial_mesh_size, max_mesh_size, mesh_expansion, mesh_contraction, mesh_scaling

1, none, 2, 0.5, RangeLog

poll

poll_pattern, polling_order, complete_poll, basis_family, basis_refresh_interval

PositiveBasis2N, Consecutive, false, RandomOrtho, 1

search_strategy, search_expansion, search_trials, search_complete

ExpandAlongSuccess, 2, 12, false

lower_bounds, upper_bounds, linear_ineq_matrix/rhs, linear_eq_matrix/rhs, nonlinear_constraints, constraint_policy

none; AugmentedLagrangian

on, 10000, 1e-12

5489, true, None

PSOutcome has minimizer, minimum, status and diagnostics: iterations, evaluations, cache_hits, search_trials, search_successes, outer_iterations (augmented Lagrangian rounds), mesh_size, penalty, max_constraint_violation, last_step. The facade’s DfoOptions::pattern_search is the same PSConfig.

Programs¶

  • The poll, the search step and the mesh

  • Constraints, budgets and the cache

Checklist¶

  1. Leave the rotating basis (RandomOrtho) on unless the coordinate axes are meaningful.

  2. Keep the search step on for smooth functions.

  3. Give bounds whenever you know them: they enable the scaling and keep every trial in range.

  4. Write linear restrictions as matrices, not as nonlinear constraints; they are enforced exactly.

  5. For equalities and the most accurate boundary answers, use AugmentedLagrangian; for the cheapest feasible answer, ExtremeBarrier.

  6. Read status, then max_constraint_violation.
